translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Nick’s lyrical, reserved, retrospective voice and the brittle brightness of the dialogue are rendered in natural literary Vietnamese; the 1920s songs are short rhymed lyrics keeping their line counts.
decisions.rationale: The book’s effect depends on tone and rhythm.

decisions.decision: ‘anh’ in Jordan’s narration always means Nick; Nick says ‘tôi’; Tom and Nick use ‘anh/tôi’; Myrtle is ‘chị Wilson’ in narration.
decisions.rationale: Ambiguous pronouns were the source of several majors in the first drafts.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘of Chicago’ was turned into the wedding’s location; the speaker and addressee of unit 729 were inverted; the rain and voices simile (723) was lost; the Sheik song (615) lost its meaning and rhyme; and ‘anh’ in Jordan’s narration was ambiguous (601–613); all corrected.
‘I’m not?’ became ‘Không sao?’ and lost its meaning; now ‘Tôi không chăm sóc cô ấy nữa à?’.
Nick’s question ‘Anh chắc là muốn em đi chứ?’ read as spoken by Daisy; it is ‘…muốn tôi đi chứ?’.
Catherine was written as Myrtle’s elder sister (units 1407, 1459 and 213); she is the younger.
Missing verb, lexical slips, addressee errors and calques in the early chapters were corrected over three rounds.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: Gatsby’s verbal tic, rendered identically at every occurrence.

glossary.source_term: the valley of ashes / West Egg / East Egg
glossary.draft_rendering: Thung lũng Tro / West Egg / East Egg
glossary.rationale: The valley of ashes is translated and the two Eggs are kept as names.
The source prints ‘Wolfshiem’; the Vietnamese uses the standard spelling ‘Wolfsheim’ except in the letter’s printed signature.
Catherine is Myrtle’s younger sister; a first draft had made her the elder.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #64317, an electronic transcription of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (New York: Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1925). The Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated; it prints the name of Meyer Wolfsheim as ‘Wolfshiem’, which is kept in the source and signature but rendered in the Vietnamese as ‘Wolfsheim’.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The Southern drunk-speech spellings in units 434–441 are rendered with only light marking.

title_review.rationale: The Vietnamese title ‘Gatsby vĩ đại’ is this edition’s own rendering; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The last line: boats against the current.
